title: Langos
subtitle: Hungarian deep-fried flatbread with garlic cream
excerpt: A soft, yeasted dough is stretched thin and deep-fried until puffed and golden, then spread generously with garlic soured cream. Langos is Hungary's most popular street food. The word comes from 'lang', meaning flame -- originally baked beside bread ovens.
sourceNotes: Langos is Hungary's most popular street food. Sold at markets and lakeshore stands, it is deep-fried and topped with soured cream and grated cheese. The word comes from 'lang', meaning flame -- originally baked in bread ovens beside the fire.

content.text: Langos uses a baking powder dough rather than yeast, so no proving time is needed. The dough is a little sticky -- that is correct. Use well-floured hands to stretch it. Eat immediately while hot.

items.prepNote: crushed, mixed into the soured cream

content.text: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Pour in the warm milk and mix to a soft, sticky dough. Rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces. Using well-floured hands, stretch and flatten each piece into a thin disc about 20cm wide.
Heat sunflower oil in a deep saucepan to 175°C. Test with a small piece of dough -- it should sizzle immediately.
Fry each disc for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and puffed. Drain on kitchen paper.
Stir crushed garlic into the soured cream. Spread generously over the hot langos and serve immediately.

items.fix: Test with a small piece of dough -- it should sizzle immediately. Use a thermometer if possible.

content.text: Hungary's street food scene. Sold at the Balaton lakeside, Christmas markets, and village fairs. Eaten hot, topped with garlic soured cream and sometimes grated cheese. The definitive Hungarian fast food.
